intent: Stop brings a live run to a settled terminal state during generation, tool work, and command execution, and Continue resumes without replaying an uncertain action.
steps: Start an approved run inside one writable folder with a long task that streams model output, queues tool work, and runs an allowlisted verifier command.
Press Stop while the model is still streaming and inspect the trace and the transcript.
Restart the run and press Stop while a queued tool request is waiting to execute.
Restart the run and press Stop while an allowlisted command is actively running.
Restart the run and press Stop immediately after a patch has been applied but before its result is recorded as settled.
Choose Continue after each cancellation and observe where the run resumes.
Let the lease expire without pressing Stop and then ask the run to take the next action a model already proposed.
expectedOutcome: Stop settles model generation, any queued tool work, and any active command, and reaches one visible terminal state in every case.
The run trace preserves the requests, approvals, bounded results, cancellation, failures, and patch identities that existed at the moment of the Stop.
Patch and checkpoint state is preserved so an applied patch remains revertible through the drift-checked revert path.
Continue restarts from the last settled boundary and re-asks or re-proposes anything that was left uncertain.
An expired or revoked lease prevents the next action even when a model has already proposed it.
Relaunching the app after a cancellation recovers the conversation at the same settled boundary.
mustNotHappen: Stop never leaves a model stream, a queued tool request, or an active command running in the background after the run reports it stopped.
Continue never silently replays an action whose outcome was uncertain at cancellation, and never applies a patch or command twice.
A cancelled or expired run never takes one further action on a model proposal made before the Stop.
Cancellation never discards the run trace, the applied patch record, or the checkpoint needed to revert.
Cancellation never widens authority, and never leaves a partially applied patch outside the writable root.
